articles.title: Shohei Ohtani out of Dodgers lineup for third straight game as possible IL stint looms
articles.summary: It's unclear when Shohei Ohtani will be appearing for the Dodgers again.
articles.body:
Shohei Ohtani's absence from the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup has reached a third straight game, with the possibility of an injured list stint seemingly becoming more real with each day.

Ohtani was once again out of the lineup for the Dodgers' game against the Washington Nationals on Saturday. Dalton Rushing was originally the replacement at designated hitter, but he was later scratched and replaced by Alex Call.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters later Saturday that Ohtani will hit in the cage, per The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya , with his body's response deciding the next course of action, such as the IL.

Ohtani's last appearance in a game was on Wednesday, an ugly four-strikeout performance that sparked new concerns that the knee issue that has kept him off the mound since early July is starting to affect his hitting. He has slashed only .264/.344/.526 in the two months he's worked only as a designated hitter, well off his norms since joining the Dodgers, and remains only two for his last 23, with 11 strikeouts.

Roberts has gotten progressively less optimistic about Ohtani's outlook over the past few days, conceding that an IL stint was a "possibility" on Wednesday then admitting he was "hopeful" but not "confident" Ohtani would avoid such a fate .

The possibility of Ohtani returning as a pitcher appears more remote, with Roberts saying earlier this week that shutting him down for the season on the mound is "an option."

If Ohtani hits the injured list, it will be the first time he's done so since joining the Dodgers before the 2024 season. Even while recovering from internal brace surgery on the torn UCL in his pitching arm, he was still playing nearly every day as a designated hitter.

MLB rules state that injured list placements can only be backdated a maximum of three days. The Dodgers would obviously like to have Ohtani in their lineup as soon as possible, but the question will soon be whether they want to bet an entire roster spot on him becoming healthy enough within a week.

articles.title: Yankees' Trent Grisham goes on IL with right hamstring strain as Aaron Judge nears return
articles.summary: The Yankees have players to fill in for Grisham in the outfield, and AL MVP Aaron Judge could soon be among them.
articles.body:
Outfielder Trent Grisham has been placed on the 10-day injured list with a right hamstring strain, the New York Yankees announced on Saturday .

Grisham, 29, left Friday's 3-2 loss to the San Diego Padres in the second inning. After drawing a walk against Padres pitcher Walker Buehler, Grisham attempted to steal second base and was thrown out.

In the bottom of the second, Grisham played center field in the bottom of the inning. But he was clearly laboring while trying to run in on a bloop single by Xander Bogaerts and Spencer Jones shifted over to center field from right field in the third.

Grisham has 18 home runs, 19 doubles and 59 RBI this season, but is slashing .211/.308/.395 in 484 plate appearances. In mid-June, he also went on the IL with a right hamstring issue and was sidelined for approximately three weeks. However, Grisham told reporters that this strain was in a different spot, according to The Athletic's Chris Kirschner .

Jones will likely stay in center field for the Yankees' remaining 21 regular-season games. He's played 24 of his 61 games at that position with 16 starts. In 152 innings, advanced metrics rate him as slightly below average with -1 Defensive Runs Saved and -1 Outs Above Average. During his four-plus seasons in the minor leagues, Jones played 325 games in center.

Heliot Ramos played right field in Friday's game after Jones moved to center and he's starting there on Saturday. Ramos was picked up at the MLB trade deadline from the San Francisco Giants.

Jasson Domínguez was recalled from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre to take Grisham's spot on the Yankees roster and he could play some right field, as well. He's played 41 games there during his time with the Yankees this season. In 53 major-league games, his slash line is .230/.270/.380, while he's slashing .283/.361/.420 in the minors.

Aaron Judge to face live pitching on Monday

However, Domínguez might not be on the Yankees' roster for long if Aaron Judge is activated from the injured list. The three-time American League MVP took on-field batting practice on Friday for the first time since suffering a stress fracture in his right rib cage.

Judge also ran the bases and worked in the outfield, indicating that he could return soon. Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Judge could be activated during the team's upcoming homestand from Sept. 8-13.

The Yankees slugger said he does not want to go on a minor-league rehab assignment and Boone said he will face live pitching on Monday. In lieu of a rehab assignment, Judge may initially play partial games when he returns.

articles.title: Cardinals Support Rincon With Tilted Hats in Photos, Rockies' Goodman Denies Complaining to Ump
articles.summary: Several St. Louis Cardinals players wore their hats tilted to the side as a show of support for rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon ahead of a matchup with the Colorado Rockies on Saturday.
articles.body:
Several St. Louis Cardinals players wore their hats tilted to the side as a show of support for rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon ahead of a matchup with the Colorado Rockies on Saturday.

On Friday, home plate umpire Doug Eddings called time to speak to Rincon about straightening his tilted hat in a clash with Colorado. Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol then argued with Eddings about the situation before he was later ejected .

During the verbal altercation between Marmol and Eddings, a pitch clock violation was given to Cardinals reliever Justin Bruihl.

Marmol said that he thought Eddings' actions were "embarrassing" after the game, as Rincon was making his MLB debut.

"Quite honestly, I thought it was pretty embarrassing on his end," Marmol told reporters . "We have a kid making his debut, and in-between an at-bat, he tells him he needs to fix the hat, and 'The kid's not going to wear his hat like that on my field.' Last I checked, this is Coors Field."

"So, I took issues with it," he added. "And the pitch violation while I'm out there having the discussion, that's also stupid, in my opinion... at the end of the day, I thought they handled it poorly, and I'd like an explanation at some point."

According to Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch , Eddings said that the hat tilt was an "unwritten rule" and a Colorado batter pointed out the angle of Rincon's cap before he noticed it.

Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman, who faced Rincon to start the same inning in which the incident occurred, denied complaining about the right-hander's tilted hat.

"I never once mentioned the hat," Goodman said Saturday, per MLB.com's Thomas Harding . "It doesn't matter who's pitching. I don't care how they wear the hat. I'm trying to find out where the ball is coming out, and I'm trying to worry about what I'm doing in the box. I'm not worried about how his hat looks.

"It was one of those situations -- it's kind of a wild, wild thing that happens in the game. But I didn't like seeing that my name was a part of it today when I didn't say anything like that. You watch baseball growing up. There are a lot of guys who have had their hat crooked or however. Honestly, before today, when I went back and looked, I didn't even notice the hat was messed up or looked like that when I was hitting. Anyways, I don't pay attention to that stuff."

As the Cardinals continued their three-game series against the Rockies on Saturday, Rincon's teammates stood behind him.

articles.title: Cubs Minor League Wrap: The Smokies shut down the Lookouts, 4-0
articles.summary: Wins for Knoxville and South Bend. The penultimate Pelicans contest of 2026 was rained out.
articles.body:
Andrew Wantz started and held the Clippers to just one run on three hits over four innings. Wants walked one and struck out three.

Gavin Hollowell pitched one inning in a rehab assignment and allowed one run on two hits and two walks. He did not strike anyone out.

Shelby Miller pitched on back-to-back nights for the first time in his rehab and got the loss. Miller was charged with four runs on two hits and two walks over two-thirds of an inning. He struck out two. However . . .

I should also mention that two of the runs charged to Miller scored after he left the game.

Left fielder Chas McCormick hit a solo home run in the second inning, his 13th on the season. McCormick was a perfect 3 for 3 before he left in the eighth inning after getting hit by a pitch.

Third baseman Owen Miller was 2 for 5 with one run driven in and one run scored.

Center fielder Justin Dean was 2 for 3 with a walk and a stolen base. He scored twice.

Dawson Netz and Tyler Schlaffer combined on a three-hit shutout. Netz pitched five innings and got the win after allowing just two hits. He struck out nine and walked two.

Schlaffer finished the game with the four-inning save. Schlaffer allowed just one hit and two walks while striking out seven.

So yeah, the Smokies two pitchers combined for 16 strikeouts.

Right fielder Alex Ramírez went 3 for 4 with a two-run double in the fourth.

Left fielder Carter Trice hit an RBI double in the eighth inning. Then he stole third base and scored on a bad throw. Trice went 1 for 4.

First baseman Miguel Useche was 2 for 4.

Dominick Reid was strong in his High-A debut, giving South Bend four scoreless innings on two hits. Reid struck out four and did not walk anyone.

The win went to Pierce Coppola in relief. Coppola gave up a run in the eighth and a run in the ninth. His final line was two runs on seven hits over 3.2 innings. Coppola struck out two and walked no one, but he did hit two batters.

JP Wheat was summoned from the pen to get South Bend's final out and pick up the save. Wheat faced two batters. He hit the first one and struck out the second, which sounds like a perfect Wheat outing.

Shortstop Angel Cepeda went 2 for 3 with a walk. He drove in one run and scored one run.

Center fielder Alexey Lumpuy was 2 for 3 with a bases-loaded walk and three steals. Lumpuy scored twice.

Right fielder Michael Gupton went 2 for 4 with a leadoff triple in the fifth inning. He was stranded there, but scored later on Lumpuy's bases-loaded walk.

Second baseman Jose Escobar went 2 for 3 with an RBI double and a sacrifice fly for two total RBI.

Lumpuy made a great catch in center field.

Rained out. As the season ends tomorrow and the game has no impact on playoff spots, it will not be made up.

articles.title: MLB Teams Next in Line for a New Stadium Amid Angels Rumors
articles.summary: Major League Baseball is overdue for a run on new stadiums.
articles.body:
Major League Baseball is overdue for a run on new stadiums.

If it felt like there was a new one every year for a while there, that's not totally wrong. Of the 30 active ballparks in the league today, 23 opened between 1989 and 2012. Since then, only Truist Park in Atlanta and Globe Life Field in Arlington have been added to the mix.

Times are changing, though. One club is actively building a new stadium, while another recently secured government approval for one. Several others are pursuing or teasing new stadiums, including the Los Angeles Angels following this week's $4 billion sale to Stan Kroenke.

It's clearly a good time to get a lay of the land ahead, so let's break down all the teams and cities that are next in line for a new stadium.

As of now, the Athletics' new stadium in Las Vegas is the only one that is for real happening.

In May, Mick Akers of the Las Vegas Review-Journal reported that the A's had spent $400 million out of their $2 billion allotment for the stadium, making it on time and on budget. It'll be right on the Las Vegas Strip on the corner of corner of Las Vegas Boulevard and Tropicana Avenue.

The stadium is only going to seat 33,000 fans, but a more intimate experience is the whole idea. They say that 80 percent of the seats are going to be within the foul poles, allowing for a shared view of the field with the Las Vegas skyline beyond the outfield.

The A's were a big draw in Oakland in the late 1980s and early 1990s, but less so as consistently low payrolls and gnarly conditions at the Oakland Coliseum drove fans away in the 2000s, 2010s and early 2020s. Naturally, they aren't drawing better in Sacramento since arriving last season. The only way to go from here is up.

At the same time, there has never seemed to be much demand for an MLB franchise in Las Vegas, and the A's brand doesn't exactly have the drawing power of, say, the Yankees, Dodgers, Red Sox or Cubs.

The NFL's Raiders have proved that a team can move from Oakland and find good attendance in Las Vegas, yet that has a lot to do with away fans coming to Las Vegas for a weekend. That kind of phenomenon may not translate to a 162-game baseball season that unfolds on a daily basis over six months.

This is hot off the presses, as a financing agreement for the Rays to build a new $2.3 billion stadium was only just approved last week .

The plan is to build it near Raymond James Stadium, which is about a half hour away from where the Rays currently call home at Tropicana Field. It's meant to be a stadium with at least 28,000 seats, indicating that, like the A's, the Rays are going for a more intimate feel.

Renderings for the new stadium make it look like a Mirror Universe version of Tropicana Field. Rather than dark and closed off, it looks intended to be bright and with a view of downtown Tampa beyond the outfield.

The Rays certainly hope the answer is yes. In fact, they're counting on it.

According to Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times , majority owner Patrick Zalupski is already hyping up the Rays being able to afford top-15, maybe even top-10 payrolls upon moving into their new ballpark. The Rays are usually in the bottom five of the league in payroll.

Time could actually prove Zalupski to be wise. Though the Rays have never drawn well, they're not abandoning a fanbase like the A's did. And unlike Tropicana Field, the new site will actually be in the more populous Tampa instead of the less populous St. Petersburg.

This project isn't moving forward yet, but it's another where the latest development happened recently.

In late August, the Kansas City city council approved a $600 million commitment for a new stadium that would be part of a mixed-use development near downtown Kansas City. The team is footing another $760 million, with hopes that the state will provide an additional $540 million. The goal is to break ground in 2027.

It's unclear what the capacity is meant to be, but renderings released by the team depict the new stadium as a more modern-looking Kauffman Stadium. Most notably, there will still be fountains beyond the center field wall.

In all fairness, it's not as if the Royals currently play in fan-repellent stadium akin to the ones the A's and Rays are looking to leave behind. Kauffman Stadium generally rates highly, including among Yelp reviewers .

Nonetheless, Kauffman Stadium opened in 1973 and is thus firmly on the dated side. It also hasn't exactly been a place to be in recent years, with the Royals ranking in the bottom five of the AL in attendance annually since 2022.

Simply changing the location of where the Royals play home games could help bump the numbers up. Kauffman Stadium is not in downtown Kansas City, whereas the new site would be much closer in the Crown Center area.

MLB Fans Assemble Giant Hot Dog in Stands ▶️

The prospect of the White Sox building a new stadium in the proposed "The 78" neighborhood of Chicago first popped up in 2024, but it was a dream at that point as much as anything else. Plenty of renderings . No solid plan.

Now the ball is moving in the right direction, courtesy of future White Sox owner ( it's complicated ) Justin Ishbia.

As reported by Jon Greenberg of The Athletic on Saturday, Canal Edge, a development company controlled by Ishbia, announced plans for a new mixed-use development in the South Loop with a new White Sox stadium as its centerpiece. The proposed site is next to the Chicago River and is meant to be "integrated into the surrounding neighborhood fabric, with programmable open space, retail, and dining designed to activate the area 365 days a year."

Anything would be an upgrade over Rate Field. It opened in 1991, the year before Oriole Park at Camden Yards kicked off a wave of retro stadiums that felt like destinations as much as ballparks. The White Sox missed the boat.

If the White Sox do get a stadium at Ishbia's proposed site, there would be at least one major advantage beyond the newness of it all. The South Loop neighborhood is closer to the heart of Chicago, potentially making the new home of the White Sox a hot spot with greater access to more people.

The interesting thing is that the new site would move the White Sox closer to Wrigley Field. That potentially sets up a sort of turf war between the White Sox and Cubs for fans, which would heighten an already intense local rivalry.

Don't read too much into recent headlines boldly proclaiming that the Angels' owner-in-waiting, Stan Kroenke, already has plans to build a new stadium.

Those headlines stem from a report from Barry M. Bloom of Forbes that was subsequently corrected like so: "Information about building a new ballpark was removed from this story on Wednesday because a spokesperson for Kroenke said the Angels were not ready to move forward on the project at this time, but might in the future."

Still, this will do for a hint that Kroenke has a new stadium on his mind. It's definitely time for one, as Angel Stadium is 60 years old and not especially beloved.

Even sans solid plans for a new stadium, it already feels like a given that things are looking up for the Angels franchise.

Whereas Arte Moreno was a truly singular disaster as an owner, Kroenke's teams in the NFL, NBA and NHL have won championships. Once he's able to remake the franchise in his image, the Angels should go from being a perennial embarrassment to regular contenders.

As is, the franchise has the benefit of MLB's second-biggest market and the fifth-best attendance among AL clubs even amid one of the worst years in club history. Give this fanbase a new stadium, and the numbers can only go up.

Fair to Ask: Diamondbacks, Guardians, Blue Jays

As recently as 2022, Diamondbacks owner Ken Kendrick was openly musing about the possibility of a new stadium in the Phoenix area. Chase Field isn't that old, but it does feel dated and is not particularly well liked.

As of 2025, the D-backs are nonetheless supposed to remain at Chase Field for another 30 years after Arizona governor Katie Hobbs signed a bill that appropriates $500 million for renovations. Yet as Zach Buchanan of Axios reported, negotiations over the actual lease have grown contentious since then.

Stadium Status: Progressive Field since 1994

The Guardians have already gone the renovations route with Progressive Field, unveiling new improvements in 2024 and 2025. Those have helped modernize a ballpark that started as retro and was beginning to feel more like just plain old.

Yet since Progressive Field is MLB's 10th-oldest stadium, the relative oldness is still a thing. Maybe it won't happen soon, but the Guardians belong on list of teams to eye for a new stadium after the A's, Rays, Royals, White Sox and Angels get theirs.

Stadium Status: Rogers Centre since 1989

Like the Guardians, the Blue Jays have taken to renovating the Rogers Centre. It was a $400 million project undertaken between 2022 and 2024, and the stadium's aesthetics and general vibe are definitely better for it.

Yet as Blue Jays president Mark Shapiro said in 2022, the Rogers Centre renovations are "a medium-term solution." Rogers Centre is the sixth-oldest stadium in MLB, so it should just be a matter of time before concrete plans for a new ballpark are drawn up.

MLB commissioner Rob Manfred has talked a lot about expansion in recent years, and Maury Brown of Forbes recently cited three cities that "may currently have a bit of a leg up compared to the competition." Nashville is one of them. There is an organized effort to bring an MLB team, as well as a solid idea for a new stadium .

Salt Lake City is another of the three cities that may have an edge on other possible expansion sites. There's already a proposal for a $1.8 billion stadium and, just this past week, Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune reported on how Utah's bid for an MLB team "has only gained momentum."

Portland is the third city that may be ahead of all the others in pushing for an expansion team. In 2025, Oregon governor Tina Kotek signed a bill that authorizes up to $800 million for a new stadium. There are renderings for what it would look like on a piece of riverfront property on the Willamette River.

Orlando is a booming market, and it was even floated as a possible alternative for the Rays before they secured a deal for a new stadium in Tampa. The "Orlando Dreamers" project reportedly has $1.5 billion committed to team ownership and another $1 billion for a new stadium.

The Montreal Expos still live on social media , and there is a movement to bring them back . Baseball in Montreal famously did not work out the first time, but perhaps it's time to try again. The area has 4.4 million people living in it, and Olympic Stadium is still there and undergoing major renovations .

articles.title: Watch MLB Fans Put Giant Flying Hot Dog Into Giant Bun in Trending Video from Royals vs. Blue Jays
articles.summary: The Kansas City Royals may be having a season to forget, but their fans are certainly still having fun.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Royals may be having a season to forget, but their fans are certainly still having fun.

And how could they not when they successfully put a giant flying hot dog in a bun during Saturday's game against the Toronto Blue Jays:

Kansas City fans at Kauffman Stadium were separately bouncing around a large bun and large hot dog like beach balls at Kauffman Stadium on Saturday when they decided to bring them together. The crowd reacted with immediate joy upon the successful completion of the task, which was caught on video.

It also provided the fans more joy than the Royals, who lost 4-3 and fell to 63-80 as the last-place team in the American League Central.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani Going on IL Would 'Be More of a Deterrent' amid Injury Rehab, Says Dodgers Manager
articles.summary: There aren't many downsides to having a two-way star who hits and pitches like Shohei Ohtani on your roster, but the Los Angeles Dodgers could be facing one after the four-time MVP missed his third straight game with left knee and right biceps discomfort.
articles.body:
There aren't many downsides to having a two-way star who hits and pitches like Shohei Ohtani on your roster, but the Los Angeles Dodgers could be facing one after the four-time MVP missed his third straight game with left knee and right biceps discomfort.

Since Ohtani is designated as a two-way player, he has to go on the injured list for a minimum of 15 days instead of 10.

"That'd be more of a deterrent," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Saturday of potentially placing him on the IL, per Doug Padilla of the Associated Press.

Los Angeles could backdate the IL stint a maximum of three days if it does decide to make that move, but it would still be a significant amount of time without one of the best players in the league.

There was some progress, though, as Padilla noted Roberts said Ohtani took swings in the batting cages Saturday after not doing so the previous two days and did not report feeling discomfort.

"I feel that it's gotten a lot better given his demeanor the last couple days," Roberts said. "What I have learned about Shohei is when he doesn't feel well, physically, he gets more short, and it's just not the same personality, which makes sense. And so I think the last couple days he's gotten a lot more loose and easygoing."

Ohtani has not pitched since July 3 as the Dodgers manage his health and has struggled of late hitting just .137 with one home run in his last 13 games. Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong has seized control of the National League MVP race in the meantime with Ohtani not pitching or hitting like himself.

Still, the Dodgers will surely need the six-time All-Star back and healthy if they are going to win a third straight World Series title.

While a starting rotation that features Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow gives them plenty of remaining starpower on the mound, Ohtani is an elite hitter who can carry the offense throughout October.

He launched eight home runs in 17 postseason games last year and took home the National League Championship Series MVP in the win over the Milwaukee Brewers.

It remains to be seen whether the Dodgers will place Ohtani on the 15-day injured list, but they have a commanding 10.5-game lead in the National League West and will need him ready to go come playoff time as they look to remain atop the sport's mountaintop.

articles.title: Umpire Doug Eddings apologizes to Cardinals pitcher Hansel Rincon for telling him to straighten crooked cap
articles.summary: Eddings stopped play in the middle of an at-bat during Friday's game to tell the rookie hurler to fix his tilted cap.
articles.body:
Umpire Doug Eddings apologized to St. Louis Cardinals pitcher Hancel Rincon on Saturday for telling the rookie to straighten his tilted cap during Friday's 7-6 win over the Colorado Rockies.

Eddings' directive to Rincon caused an uproar that resulted in Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol being ejected from the game for arguing over what occurred.

"He apologized for what happened [Friday] night," Rincon said through bullpen catcher and team interpreter Kleininger Teran, via the St. Louis Post Dispatch's Derrick Goold . "He also told me good luck for the rest of my career as a big-leaguer."

The rookie added that he told Eddings, "'Don't worry, it's nothing personal, and everything stays here," according to MLB.com's Owen Perkins .

The incident in question occurred during the sixth inning of Friday's game as Rincon made his major-league debut. As the rookie was pitching to Colorado's Cole Carrigg, Eddings called timeout and appeared to tell Rincon (through Cardinals catcher Leo Bernal) to straighten the brim of his cap.

Rincon had already given up a triple to TJ Rumfield and thrown a wild pitch that allowed the Rockies first baseman to score. Following Eddings' stoppage, the right-hander then threw a 96 mph fastball right down the middle of the strike zone that Carrigg hit off the wall in right-center field for an eventual inside-the-park home run .

After that, Rincon allowed a single to Connor Norby and he was replaced by Justin Bruihl. He finished with three runs and three hits allowed in 1/3 of an inning. As Bruihl warmed up, Marmol came out to argue with Eddings and was ejected from the game.

Following the game, Eddings told reporters that Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman raised the issue of Rincon's cap , asking if it could be worn that way. The umpire acknowledged that Rincon was not breaking any MLB rule . However, Goodman denied saying anything.

"I never once mentioned the hat," Goodman said, via MLB.com's Thomas Harding . "It doesn't matter who's pitching. I don't care how they wear the hat. I'm trying to find out where the ball is coming out, and I'm trying to worry about what I'm doing in the box. I'm not worried about how his hat looks."

Before Saturday's game, which St. Louis lost 10-7 , Eddings talked to Marmol and Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer, then made sure to speak with Rincon as the Cardinals pitchers walked to the bullpen.

During batting practice, most of the Cardinals players wore their caps with the brim turned to the left in protest. Many of them continued to wear their caps crooked, as did several Rockies players, during the game. Several Cardinals fans behind home plate and radio broadcaster John Rooney also wore their caps with a crooked brim in solidarity.

"I felt big support from my teammates," Rincon said . "Obviously, when you are together, like this group, we're gonna be much better."

Rincon also pitched in Saturday's game, allowing four runs and two hits in one inning. In addition to inspiring a fashion statement during his brief MLB career, the rookie has compiled a 47.25 ERA in his two outings.

articles.title: Max Kepler DFA'd by D-Backs, Top Potential Landing Spots for MLB Playoff Races
articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks announced Sunday they designated veteran outfielder Max Kepler for assignment.
articles.body:
The Arizona Diamondbacks announced Sunday they designated veteran outfielder Max Kepler for assignment.

The 33-year-old missed the first half of the 2026 MLB season through suspension and signed with Arizona in early June. He struggled mightily out west, putting up a .205/.262/.303 slash line in 41 appearances.

It's reasonable to conclude Kepler's suspension has impacted his performance, but he wasn't exactly lighting it up in previous years. Just once since 2020 has he finished with an OPS+ higher than 100, which represents the league average, per Baseball Reference .

With Sunday's move, another team will have the opportunity to add Kepler for the stretch run.

The Chicago White Sox could be one option after they just announced they placed Tommy Pham on the 10-day injured list.

The San Diego Padres make theoretical sense given their lack of depth and paucity of options on the left side of the plate. They took a flier on Austin Hays despite him having a .576 OPS with the White Sox, and signing Kepler wouldn't be any different from that.

The Boston Red Sox are in a similar bind. Masataka Yoshida remains sidelined with a hamstring injury , and they have no left-handers they can bring off the bench for a platoon advantage.

Granted, the hitting splits don't help Kepler's case for being a late-season signing. He's slugging just .283 against right-handed pitching and has struck out more times (29) than he got hits (23).

Unsung heroes always emerge around this time of the year. In the case of Kepler, it's hard to find any evidence supporting the idea he'll improve with a change of scenery.

Should he want to continue his career, he may have to wait until next spring to get his next MLB chance.

articles.title: Cardinals make decision on rookie pitcher days after Doug Eddings incident
articles.summary: St. Louis Cardinals right-handed pitcher Hancel Rincon had an incident with umpire Doug Eddings on Friday.
articles.body:
As rosters expanded to 28 players on Tuesday, the St. Louis Cardinals used one of their extra spots to call up right-handed pitcher Hancel Rincon from Triple-A Memphis. The 24-year-old made his MLB debut Friday.

In that game against the Colorado Rockies, Rincon entered the game to start the bottom of the sixth inning. He had already faced two batters and got into a 2-0 count on a third when umpire Doug Eddings told him to adjust his hat.

Rincon was wearing it off to the side, and after complying with Eddings' demand, allowed an inside-the-park home run to Rockies center fielder Cole Carrigg.

Rincon faced four batters in total before being lifted from the game. Cardinals manager Oli Marmol was frustrated with Eddings since the hat incident a few minutes prior, and was ejected following the pitching change.

Sep 4, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; St. Louis Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol (37) argues with home plate umpire Doug Eddings (88) in the sixth inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The next day, St. Louis players wore their hats to the side in protest. According to their broadcast, some Colorado players did as well. Eddings apologized to Rincon for his actions from the previous night before the game.

The 24-year-old got into Saturday's game, throwing the sixth inning again. He allowed four runs on two hits and a walk while picking up his first MLB strikeout. Overall, Rincon had a rocky weekend in Denver. He surrendered seven earned runs in 1 ⅓ innings pitched, walking one and striking out one.

The scuffle with Eddings happened close to the start of his Friday appearance, which might have impacted his performance. Ahead of Sunday's game, Rincon was demoted to Triple-A with lefty long man Cooper Hjerpe coming up to MLB.

The 25-year-old was taken in the first round of the 2022 draft by the Cardinals, but has struggled with injury during his minor league career. He sat out all of 2025 with Tommy John Surgery, but has pitched well since his return earlier this season.

In five starts and 19 innings at Memphis, Hjerpe has pitched to a 0.95 ERA, striking out 27 and walking 17. He has always been a high-strikeout high-walk guy, but these numbers do jump off the page.

Pitchers usually struggle with command after coming back from TJ, so hopefully that is all it is. He will now be working with an MLB staff as the Cardinals (70-70) attempt to make a run for the third National League Wild Card spot.

articles.title: Umpire Doug Eddings apologizes to Cardinals pitcher Hansel Rincon after MLB reportedly reprimanded him for telling rookie to straighten crooked cap
articles.summary: Eddings stopped play in the middle of an at-bat during Friday's game to tell the rookie hurler to fix his tilted cap.
articles.body:
Umpire Doug Eddings apologized to St. Louis Cardinals pitcher Hancel Rincon on Saturday for telling the rookie to straighten his tilted cap during Friday's 7-6 win over the Colorado Rockies.

However, the veteran umpire reportedly felt compelled to do so after Major League Baseball told him that he acted inappropriately in admonishing Rincon, according to The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal .

Eddings' directive to Rincon caused an uproar that resulted in Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol being ejected from the game for arguing over what occurred.

"He apologized for what happened [Friday] night," Rincon said through bullpen catcher and team interpreter Kleininger Teran, via the St. Louis Post Dispatch's Derrick Goold . "He also told me good luck for the rest of my career as a big-leaguer."

The rookie added that he told Eddings, "'Don't worry, it's nothing personal, and everything stays here," according to MLB.com's Owen Perkins .

The incident in question occurred during the sixth inning of Friday's game as Rincon made his major-league debut. As the rookie was pitching to Colorado's Cole Carrigg, Eddings called timeout and appeared to tell Rincon (through Cardinals catcher Leo Bernal) to straighten the brim of his cap.

Rincon had already given up a triple to TJ Rumfield and thrown a wild pitch that allowed the Rockies first baseman to score. Following Eddings' stoppage, the right-hander then threw a 96 mph fastball right down the middle of the strike zone that Carrigg hit off the wall in right-center field for an eventual inside-the-park home run .

After that, Rincon allowed a single to Connor Norby and he was replaced by Justin Bruihl. He finished with three runs and three hits allowed in 1/3 of an inning. As Bruihl warmed up, Marmol came out to argue with Eddings and was ejected from the game.

Following the game, Eddings told reporters that Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman raised the issue of Rincon's cap , asking if it could be worn that way. The umpire acknowledged that Rincon was not breaking any MLB rule . However, Goodman denied saying anything.

"I never once mentioned the hat," Goodman said, via MLB.com's Thomas Harding . "It doesn't matter who's pitching. I don't care how they wear the hat. I'm trying to find out where the ball is coming out, and I'm trying to worry about what I'm doing in the box. I'm not worried about how his hat looks."

Before Saturday's game, which St. Louis lost 10-7 , Eddings talked to Marmol and Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer, then made sure to speak with Rincon as the Cardinals pitchers walked to the bullpen. This reportedly occurred after MLB told Eddings that he went too far by telling Rincon to straighten his cap.

It's uncertain whether or not Eddings could be disciplined further by MLB for the incident, Rosenthal reports.

During batting practice, most of the Cardinals players wore their caps with the brim turned to the left in protest. Many of them continued to wear their caps crooked, as did several Rockies players, during the game. Several Cardinals fans behind home plate and radio broadcaster John Rooney also wore their caps with a crooked brim in solidarity.

"I felt big support from my teammates," Rincon said . "Obviously, when you are together, like this group, we're gonna be much better."

Rincon also pitched in Saturday's game, allowing four runs and two hits in one inning. In addition to inspiring a fashion statement during his brief MLB career, the rookie has compiled a 47.25 ERA in his two outings.
